$comment: TF-C50 (D-LK-ARM64-ELF-RELOC-EXTERN-DISPATCH + D-ML7-2.9): a DIRECT call to an undefined extern function. In an arm64 RELOCATABLE .o this lowers to a plain BL + R_AARCH64_CALL26 (foreign linker inserts the veneer) with the dead callee-address lea suppressed -- witnessed structurally by test_elf_writer's ObjectExternCallEmitsUndefImportNameAndCall26RelocOnAarch64 pin + the foreign gcc-PIE/qemu probe. THIS runnable example proves the direct extern call RUNS end-to-end on each shipped target: abs(argc-43) with argc==1 -> abs(-42) == 42 -> exit 42. `argc` (runtime) blocks const-folding so the `release` arm exercises the real BL/CALL, not a folded literal. RED-ON-DISABLE: a mis-materialized callee makes the call land elsewhere -> not 42.

optimizedPipelines.label: full-release-like
optimizedPipelines.$commentByteIdentical: MEASURED 2026-08-15 — optimized image BYTE-IDENTICAL to the baseline on: arm64:elf64-aarch64-linux-exec, x86_64:elf64-x86_64-linux-exec. Legs actually run: windows/pe64-x86_64 and linux/elf64 (x86_64 + aarch64 under qemu); the darwin/macho64 leg was NOT run. Where the image is identical the arm's exit-code/stdout comparison is x==x and cannot fail. HONEST: the work this example pins happens behind an EXTERN call the pipeline cannot see through, so no pass has a body to transform on this side of the call. The value comes from libc `abs` applied to a runtime `argc`. Deliberately NOT given "mustDifferFromBaseline" — an honest no-op, not a missed opt-in.
